summary.text: Daniel McDow is the Democratic candidate for the Florida House of Representatives, District 33, in the November 3, 2026 general election, against Republican incumbent Monique Miller.
A former West Melbourne city councilman, he described in a Ballotpedia survey a career in contract negotiation for healthcare and publishing corporations.

paragraphs.text: McDow was born in Chicago, Illinois, earned a high school diploma from Lakeview High School, and received a graduate degree from Lincoln International Business School in 2023, according to Ballotpedia.
Ballotpedia lists his career experience as a businessman and in supply chain oversight and contract negotiation.
In a Ballotpedia survey, McDow said he is a former city councilman, chair of Parks & Recreation, and county party chair.
He ran in the 2024 Democratic primary for Florida's 8th Congressional District and lost to Sandy Kennedy.
McDow listed accountability and transparency, fiscal responsibility, freedom and equality, and lowering the cost of living, including utility and insurance costs, as his key campaign messages.
He said he supports balancing environmental, economic, and social concerns, which he called the triple bottom line.
